Mr.  Joshua  Freeman,  North  Carolina. - 

Our  very  dear  friend,  and  worthy  Brother,  Joftiua  Free¬ 
man,  departed  this  life,  Monday  evening  the  icth  of  Nov. 
1794,  in  the  59th  year  of  his  age..  For  the  piety  of  his 
life,  the  fpirituality  of  his  converfation,  and  the  extraordi¬ 
nary  fervor  of  his  zeal,  he  was  refpedted  by  all  his  acquaint¬ 
ance,  and  his  memory  deferves  to  be  perpetuated.  He  was 
born  in  Chowan  county,  North  Carolina;  his  parents  were 
ftridl  Epifcopalians.  Joftiua  was  converted  under  the  mi- 
niftry  of  our  dear  departed  brother  Jeremiah  Dargon  % 
about  17  years  ago,  and  was  received  a  member  of  his 
church  (which  is  now  under  the  care  of  the  Rev.  Robert 
Hendry),  and  became  a  Deacon  of  that  Society.  He  fear cely 
ever  heard  a  fermon  delivered  pathetically  but  he  was  ready 
to  break  out  in  praifing  and  glorifying  Cod.  His  depot  tr 
ment  was  fo  very  affectionate  and  zealous,  that  he  gained 
the  love  of  all  the  affociation.  The  brethren  thought  them- 
fel  ves  happy  when  he  Was  prefent,  and  theie  feemed  fome- 
thing  wanting  when  he  was  abfent.  He  pofiefted  aconiiderable 
fortune,  and  fome  years  paft  was  captain  of  a  company  of 
militia,  in  Bertie  county,  North  Carolina,  but  refigned  his 
office.  It  was  evident  that  he  fought  not  honor  from  man, 
but  that  which  comes  from  God  only.  He  had  many  Haves, 
but  his  lenity  towards  them  was  remarkable.  If  any  of  them 
tranfgrefled,  his  general  method  of  punifhment  was  to  ex- 
pofe  their  faults  before  the  reft  and  the  whole  family,  when 
they  were  affembled  at  morning-prayer.  His  exhortations, 
rebukes,  and  prayers  had  more  effeCl  upon  their  future  con- 
du£l  than  if  they  had  been  whipped,  or  in  any  other  way 
treated  feverel.y’t  At  the  time  of  family  worfhip,  he  was 
often  deeply  concerned  for  the  fpiritual  welfare  of  his  domef- 
tics,  and  his  zeal  was  not  the  impulfe  of  a  moment,  but 
continued  to  the  laft.  Some  time  before  his  death  he  feemed 
very  much  refigned  to  the  will  of  the  Lord,  and  greatly 
weaned  from  the  concerns  of  this  life.  He  was  feldom  heard 
to  fay  any  thing  relative  to  his  worldly  bufinefs,  but  his 
conftant  converfation  was  about  divine  things.  On  Saturday 
evening,  the  8th  of  Nov.  he  went  to  prayer  with  his  family, 
and  was  immediately  after  taken  with  a  fit  of  the  paralytic 
kind,  a  complaint  under  which  he  had  laboured  about  twelve 
months.  He  continued  languifhing  through  the  Lord’s- 
day,  and  till  Monday  evening,  when  he  died.  His  death 

js  fincerely  lamented  by  all  his  friends  and  connexions.

THE  MANNER  OF  BEATIFYING  A  SAINT  IN  ITALY. 

Ancona,  Sept.  2,  1793. 

As  I  am  now  in  a  country  where  miracles  are  wrought,  I  will 
give  you  a  little  account  of  fome  of  their  proceedings,  which 
hav'e  come  within  my  knowledge.
